turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
The README already points to `internal/mapengine/`. Let me look at its structure and the routing logic directly.I now have the full picture. Here's the answer.

## Structural map engine — location

**`internal/mapengine/`** (Go package `mapengine`), consisting of:

- **`types.go`** — public API, options/result types, and the routing logic (`Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`)
- **`goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper`, backed by Go's own `go/ast` + `go/token`
- **`treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper`, backed by `gotreesitter` (tree-sitter grammars/queries)
- **`regex.go`** — `RegexMapper`, line-pattern-based fallback for everything else
- **`regex_test.go`** — tests for the regex mapper

All three mappers implement a common `Mapper` interface (`internal/mapengine/types.go:47`):
```go
type Mapper interface {
    Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error)
}
```

## Engine selection per file

The selection happens in `mapengine.Map` → `mapAuto`, `internal/mapengine/types.go:125-158`:

```go
func Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    opts = NormalizeOptions(opts)
    switch opts.Engine {
    case EngineRegex:
        return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
    case EngineTreeSitter:
        return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, true)
    case EngineAuto:
        return mapAuto(path, content, opts)
    default: // unknown value → regex fallback with a warning
        ...
    }
}

func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
    case ".go":
        result, err := GoASTMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
        if err == nil { return result, nil }
        // parse failure → regex fallback, Result.Fallback = true
        fallback, _ := RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
        fallback.Fallback = true
        return fallback, nil
    case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
        return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, false)
    default:
        return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
    }
}
```

So selection is **by file extension** (default/auto mode):
- `.go` → `GoASTMapper` (falls back to regex silently if `go/ast` parsing errors)
- `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `TreeSitterMapper` (falls back to regex on tree-sitter error; only warns if the error isn't `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`)
- everything else → `RegexMapper` directly

It can also be forced explicitly via `Options.Engine` (`auto` | `regex` | `tree-sitter`; there's no explicit `go-ast` override path in the switch — only reachable through `auto`+`.go`).

`mapTreeSitterWithFallback` (`types.go:160-172`) is the shared fallback wrapper used both when tree-sitter is forced and when auto-routed, calling `TreeSitterMapper{}.Map` then falling back to `RegexMapper` on any error.

## Wiring into the CLI

- `internal/ghx/read.go:187-196` — the `Read()` function calls `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: opts.MapEngine, Level: opts.MapLevel, Kind: opts.MapKind})` when `--map` is passed, and reports back which engine actually ran (`result.MapEngine`) plus any fallback warnings.
- `internal/cli/ghx.go:110-121` — the `--map-engine`, `--level`, and `--kind` CLI flags are read and threaded into `ReadOpts`, which flows into `mapengine.Options`.

## Not verified

- I did not read `treesitter.go`'s internals in full (grammar/query config per language, `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs`) beyond its symbol map — only confirmed it exists and is invoked for the 6 extensions above.
- I did not check `internal/mapengine/regex_test.go` or run any tests; correctness of fallback behavior is based on reading the code, not executing it.
- I did not verify whether any other caller (e.g. `internal/codemode/`) invokes `mapengine.Map` with different options than the CLI path.

README:
# ghx — the code-reconnaissance sidecar for AI agents

**Expensive main agents shouldn't burn frontier tokens on tree/grep/read loops.**
ghx is a cheap, specialized **sidecar agent** that a main agent delegates code
reconnaissance to. Ask it a repo question in plain English; it explores GitHub
under the hood and hands back a **schema-validated evidence report** — claims
with citations, the commands it ran, and what it could not confirm — while every
artifact of the investigation lands on disk under `~/.ghx/sessions/` for you or
the parent agent to inspect.

This is the first public cut of the **Agent Sidecar Framework**: a main agent
delegates a whole competence domain to a proficient specialist instead of loading
that domain's tools and doctrine into its own context. ghx is the proof — the
code-reconnaissance sidecar — and, underneath it, a sharp standalone GitHub
exploration CLI. The durable vision lives in
[docs/NORTH_STAR.md](docs/NORTH_STAR.md).

> ghx is two products in one binary: a **sidecar brain** you delegate to (this
> README's lead), and the **classic exploration CLI** it drives under the hood
> (documented in full further down). Use whichever fits; they share one core.

## Why a sidecar

When a main agent stops mid-task to explore code, the real cost is not the API
calls — it is the context. Exploration output floods the window, the agent loses
the thread of the engineering work, and the ~400 lines of tool doctrine it needs
to explore well are dead weight it re-pays every sessi
